title: Your first frets
summary: Move by semitones on string 6 in your selected tuning.
goal: Play frets 0–1–2–3, then 3–2–1–0 with a fresh pluck on every beat.
body:
First complete the open-string lesson. A fret raises a note by one semitone. Put your fingertip just behind the metal fret, using only enough pressure for a clear note. Suggested fingers for frets 1/2/3 are index/middle/ring. Start at 60 BPM; 40–50 gives more time. Try 70 only after comfortable repeats.

Tuning: {{tuning}}. Strings 6 → 1: {{openStrings}}. Reference A4 = {{reference}} Hz. Select your actual tuning in Settings → Instrument or in Tuner. Changing the profile updates this lesson; it does not physically tune the guitar.

In the steps, {{openExample}} (6/0) means sounding note {{openExample}}, string 6, fret 0. String 1 is the thinnest; 0 means open. Read the displayed positions for your selected tuning. Pitch labels use chromatic enharmonic names. Audio measures audible pitch and attacks, not your finger or string choice.

Use a clean input from your guitar interface, or choose the acoustic microphone/pickup source explicitly. Play one note at a time and stop the previous string. Choose Practice for a signal check and count-in. Without reliable calibration, rhythm and overall scores remain unavailable. Review measured pitch or missed-attack feedback before increasing the tempo.

first-fret.body: Move one semitone above the open note: {{positions}}.

climb.title: 3. Climb in semitones
climb.body: Play the remaining beats of bar 1: {{positions}}.

return.title: 4. Return to the open string
return.body: Bar 2 begins with a new attack on fret 3, then descends: {{positions}}.

two-bars.title: 5. Join both bars
two-bars.body: Count four beats twice. Pluck every note, including the repeated note across the barline. {{positions}}.
